theme: Miss rate when the working set outgrows the cache
title: Calling the Capacity Cliff from a Reuse-Distance Sample
strategies: trivial: emit the constant training-mean miss rate (every training row is deep in the sub-cliff regime, so this constant is near 0) -> reproduces the checker's own baseline ~0.1

greedy: ordinary least squares of missrate ~ a + b*log(N) on the visible training log alone, extrapolated arbitrarily far. Every training row sits far below the effective capacity, where the true miss rate is a tiny power-law tail dominated by finite-sample noise, so the log looks flat regardless of the true steepness -- the fitted line keeps predicting near-zero long past where the true curve has already risen to nearly 1

strong: recover the reuse-distance distribution's steepness s from the histogram alone via an order-statistic log-logistic regression (logit(empirical CDF) is linear in log(x) with slope s, a scale-free fit independent of any measured working-set size), combine it with the PUBLIC effective-capacity law K=C*A/(A+1), and emit the closed form N^s/(N^s+K^s) -- correctly placing both the location and the shape of the cliff that the small-N log alone could never reveal

headroom above strong: refine s with a robust (e.g. trimmed / weighted) fit to reduce histogram sampling variance, or blend a second-order correction to the log-logistic tail, pushing held-out error toward the finite-sample noise floor
